help.intro1: The search interface is made of three sections: **Search**, **Explore**, and **Results**. These are described in detail below.
help.intro2: You may start searching either from the **Search** section or from the **Explore** section.
help.searchDesc: This section shows your current search criteria and allows you to submit keywords to search in the library.
help.search1: Each new submission adds the entered keywords to the list of search criteria.
help.search2: To start a new search instead of adding keywords to the current search, use the **Remove Filter** button, then enter your new keywords.
help.search3: To replace an already submitted keyword, first remove it by unchecking its checkbox, then submit a new keyword.
help.search4: You may control the extent of your search by selecting where to search. The options are:
help.search5: **In Authors Or Contributors:** Search your keywords in author or contributor names.
help.search6: **In Titles:** Search your keywords in titles.
help.search7: **In All Fields:** Search your keywords in all bibliographic record fields.
help.search8: **In Documents:** Search your keywords in the text content of the available documents.
help.search9: You may use boolean operators with your keywords. For instance:
help.search10: **AND:** Finds entries that contain all specified terms. This is the default relation between terms when no operator is specified, e.g., A B is the same as A AND B.
help.search11: **OR:** Finds entries that contain any of the specified terms, e.g., A OR B.
help.search13: Boolean operators must be entered in uppercase.
help.search14: You may use logical groupings (with parentheses) to eliminate ambiguities when using multiple boolean operators, e.g., (A OR B) AND C.
help.search15: You may require exact sequences of words (with double quotes), e.g., "A B C". The default difference between word positions is 1, meaning that an entry will match if it contains the words next to each other, but a different maximum distance may be specified (with the tilde character), e.g., "Web Search"~2 allows up to 1 word between Web and Search, meaning it could match web site search as well as web search.
help.exploreDesc: This section allows you to explore categories associated with the references.
help.explore1: Categories can be used to filter your search. Check a category to add it to your search criteria and narrow your search. Your search results will then only show entries that are associated with that category.
help.explore2: Uncheck a category to remove it from your search criteria and broaden your search results.
help.explore3: The numbers shown next to the categories indicate how many entries are associated with each category in the current set of results. Those numbers will vary based on your search criteria to always describe the current set of results. Likewise, categories and whole facets will disappear when the result set has no entries associated with them.
help.explore4: An arrow icon (v) appearing next to a category indicates that subcategories are available. You may press it to expand a list of more specific categories. You may press it again later to collapse the list. Expanding or collapsing subcategories will not change your current search; this allows you to quickly explore a hierarchy of categories if desired.
help.resultsDesc: This section shows the search results. When no search criteria has been given, it shows the full content of the bibliography (up to 20 entries per page).
help.results1: Each entry of the results list is a link to its full bibliographic record. From the bibliographic record view, you may continue exploring the search results by going to previous or following records in your search results, or you may return to the list of results.
help.results3: The **Abstracts** button lets you toggle the display of abstracts within the list of search results. Enabling abstracts, however, will have no effect on results for which no abstract is available.
help.results5: The **Relevance** sort is only available after keywords have been submitted using the **Search** section.
help.results6: Categories selected in the **Explore** section have no effect on the relevance score. Their only effect is to filter the list of results.
